tips.audioAi: When on, the AI decides when to play this track as the story goes, going by its "when to play" line. When off, it only plays from the playlist and behaviors.
tips.audioType: BGM: background music that loops. Sound effect: a short one-off sound, like a door opening. Ambience: a sound that stays in the background, like rain or a crowd.
tips.cooldown: After it fires, how many turns before it can fire again. 3 means it stays quiet for the next 3 turns. 0 means no limit.
tips.maxFire: How many times it can fire in one playthrough. 1 means once, good for one-off story events. 0 means no limit.
tips.effects: What happens once the conditions are met. Add as many as you like: change a variable, switch an entry on or off, play music, notify the player, tell the AI something…
tips.keywords: The entry is only sent to the AI when one of these words comes up in the chat. Write "castle, king" and the AI only reads it when the castle is mentioned. Separate words with commas.
tips.liveCanon: Lore Shift is an extension players can install. With it, a player can change the entries and variables you allow in their own playthrough, for example replace the lord of the castle. It only affects their playthrough; your card stays the same.
tips.range: The lowest and highest value. However the AI changes it, it stays inside this range, like affection 0 to 100.
tips.reaches: How and when this entry is sent to the AI: every turn, or on keywords or conditions, and where it goes in what the AI reads.
tips.varWhen: By default the AI can always see it. You can limit it to certain openings or a scenario, so it takes no space the rest of the time.
tips.whenFires: When this behavior checks: every turn by default, or when the player says something, a variable changes or a button is pressed.
tips.onlyIf: The effects below only happen when these are true. With several conditions, choose whether all must match or any one will do. Empty means it always runs.
tips.alwaysSend: On: sent to the AI every turn. Off: only sent when a keyword comes up or its conditions match, which saves words and keeps the AI focused.
tips.excludeRecursion: If another entry's text happens to contain this entry's keywords, it won't pull this one in. Only the player and AI's chat can trigger it.
tips.preventRecursion: Once this entry is sent, its own text won't trigger other entries' keywords.
tips.secondary: A second set of words used with the keywords to narrow things down, like "must also appear" or "must not appear". Usually left empty.
tips.secondaryLogic: How the second set is checked: any one of them, all of them, none of them…
tips.sendAs: Who the AI reads it as. System: rules and background, the usual choice. User: as if the player said it. Assistant: as if the AI had said it.
tips.wholeWord: When on, only whole words count: "cat" won't match "category". Rarely needed for Chinese or Japanese.
tips.imageScope: Only use this picture in chats that started from these openings. All openings means any of them.
tips.imageUrl: Where the picture comes from: paste an image link, or pick one from your assets.
tips.aiAccess: Whether the AI can change it. Can change: the AI changes it as the story goes. Read only: the AI knows it, but only behaviors and the screen change it. Hidden: the AI doesn't know it exists.
tips.preciseStep: With precise tracking on, the most it can go up (or down) in one turn; the AI picks a number in between to fit the story.
tips.section: Where in what the AI reads this entry goes. Near the top it reads like background; placed in the chat, the closer to the newest message, the more the AI weighs it.
tips.situationEnabled: Off: the whole scenario is out of play, whatever its rule says. Turn it off to set it aside without deleting it.

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Define game state variables to track player stats, items, and story progress.
variables.noVariablesDesc: The AI reads and updates variables during gameplay using bracket syntax like [health: -10].

variables.jsonHint: Must be valid JSON (object or array). Use double quotes around field names and string values.
variables.idTaken: That ID is already used by another variable — renamed to {{id}}

player_name.name: Player name

secret.name: Player's secret
secret.rule: The player's secret. Characters in the story do not know it unless the plot exposes it; narration may hint at it but never says it for the player.

origin.name: Background
origin.rule: The background the player picked. It decides where the player starts, what they can do, and how others see them.

difficulty.name: Difficulty
difficulty.rule: The difficulty the player picked; its name says what it means (e.g. Gentle, Standard, Harsh, or whatever the creator renamed them). Follow it strictly: the harder it is, the more real failure and cost; the gentler, the fewer real setbacks.

draw.rule: Who the player drew at the start, and their situation. The story starts from there.

draws_left.name: Redraws left
draws_left.rule: The screen handles this; leave it alone.

str.name: Strength
str.rule: The player's strength, 1–10, set by the player at the start. Use it for checks and description; do not change it.

agi.name: Agility
agi.rule: The player's agility, 1–10, set by the player at the start. Use it for checks and description; do not change it.

cha.name: Charm
cha.rule: The player's charm, 1–10, set by the player at the start. Use it for checks and description; do not change it.

wit.name: Wits
wit.rule: The player's wits, 1–10, set by the player at the start. Use it for checks and description; do not change it.

points_left.name: Points left
points_left.rule: The screen handles this; leave it alone.

health.name: Health
health.rule: Health, 0–100. Goes down when hurt, up with healing or rest.

stamina.name: Stamina
stamina.rule: Stamina, 0–100. Goes down with exertion, up with food or rest.

location.name: Location
location.rule: Where the player is now, in a few words. Change it when they go somewhere new.

bag.name: Inventory
bag.rule: The inventory, a list; each item is {"name": item name, "note": one line}. When the player gets something, push one, and in the same turn set new_item to "item — one line". When used up or lost, delete its index (from 0). Don't hand out items every turn.

new_item.name: Just received
new_item.rule: What the player just got. Set it to "item — one line" in the same turn you push it into the inventory; the screen shows a popup.

unlocked_places.name: Places open
unlocked_places.rule: Ids of places the player can go (home / street / market / river / outskirts). When the story gives them a way to reach one, push its id; no duplicates.

inbox.name: Phone messages
inbox.rule: Messages on the phone, a list; each is {"from": sender, "text": message}. When someone texts the player, push one and in the same turn set new_message to "sender: one line". Keep them short, like real texts.

new_message.name: New message
new_message.rule: The message just received, "sender: one line". Set it in the same turn you push to the inbox; the screen shows a popup.

reply_draft.name: Reply being typed
reply_draft.rule: What the player is typing on the phone; leave it alone.

relations.name: Relationships
relations.rule: People the player knows, a list; each is {"name": name, "level": relationship (stranger, acquaintance, friend, trusted, close), "note": one line on where things stand}. Push when they meet someone new; merge the level and note at that index when things change. Only when the story really moves.

day.name: Day
day.rule: Which day of the story it is. The screen adds one when the player ends the day; don't add it yourself unless a night clearly passes in the story.

period.name: Time of day
period.rule: The time of day (morning, afternoon, evening). After the player does something, move it on by one as the story allows; a new day starts in the morning.

actions_left.name: Actions left today
actions_left.rule: How many things the player can still do today; the screen handles this.

roll.name: Die roll
roll.rule: The d20 the player just rolled (1–20). When the player sends a roll, judge success by it: higher is better, 1 is a disaster, 20 a triumph. Never change it or reroll.

clues.name: Clues
clues.rule: Clues the player has found, a list; each is {"name": clue, "where": where it was found}. Push one when the player really finds it, and in the same turn set new_clue to "clue — one line". Don't give too many at once.

new_clue.name: New clue
new_clue.rule: The clue just found; the screen shows a popup.

accused.name: Accused
accused.rule: Who the player accused. When they send an accusation, judge it against the truth you hold and carry on; a wrong guess costs them.

unlocked.name: Collected
unlocked.rule: Ids of things collected (photo / letter / key / badge / map / musicbox). When the player really gets one in the story, push its id and in the same turn set unlock_note to "name — one line". At most one per turn; no duplicates.

unlock_note.name: Just collected
unlock_note.rule: What was just collected; the screen shows a popup.

welcome.title: Welcome to the Full editor!
welcome.body:
I'm Mushie! This is the workshop where world cards are made.
Follow me for a lap — you'll try every important spot hands-on!

nav.title: This is the navigation
nav.body: The editor has three areas: Content for your story and rules, Presentation for visuals and sound, and Publish for your card's public face. Let's go top to bottom!

goFirstMessage.title: Start with the First Message
goFirstMessage.body: The first message is what players see the moment they enter your world. Click here to open it!

createGreeting.title: Create your first message
createGreeting.body: Click this button to create your very first opening message!

greetingContent.title: Write it here
greetingContent.body: Write your opening here — {{userMacro}} stands for the player and {{charMacro}} for the character. Multiple first messages become selectable opening routes!

goLorebook.title: Next: the Lorebook
goLorebook.body: The lorebook holds your world's knowledge. Click here to take a look!

kbBooks.title: Scenarios
kbBooks.body: This column holds the card's scenarios. The card itself is the first: everything you write goes in there, and it is shared into every scenario you add later. Add one when your story needs a second place. For now, write something into the card.

entriesAdd.title: Add an entry
entriesAdd.body: Worldbuilding, character sheets, rules — you write them all as individual entries. Click "Add" to create your first one!

entryContent.title: Title for you, content for the AI
entryContent.body: The name is just a label to keep yourself organized — the AI never sees it. What matters is the content: write the actual lore there. Add keywords, and the entry is only sent to the AI when the conversation touches that topic — precise and efficient.

goVariables.title: Now, Variables
goVariables.body: Variables track numbers that change during play. Click to check them out!

varsAdd.title: Add a variable
varsAdd.body: Affection, gold, quest progress — store them all as variables. The AI and your custom UI can read and write them. Click "Add variable" to create one!

varsFields.title: Setting up a variable
varsFields.body: Give it a display name, pick a type (number/text/switch), and set the default value each playthrough starts with. The best part is "Behavior rules": tell the AI in plain words when and how the value should change — like "gain 5 affection on an intimate moment" — and it follows along.

goBehaviors.title: Next: Behaviors
goBehaviors.body: Behaviors are your world's automation rules. Click here to enter!

behaviorsAdd.title: Add a behavior
behaviorsAdd.body: Click "Add behavior" and create a rule!

behaviorsDetail.title: How a behavior works
behaviorsDetail.body: Every behavior = When… (event) + If… (conditions) + Then… (actions). For example: when a variable changes, if affection reaches 100, then switch the BGM and unlock a new entry. Configure the three parts right here.

presentationSkip.title: Presentation: advanced stuff
presentationSkip.body: Custom UI, Audio and Assets under Presentation are advanced — building your card its own interface and soundtrack. Come back when you're comfortable; the Creator Guide has full tutorials. Skipping for now!

overviewTitle.title: Name your card
overviewTitle.body: The Overview is your card's public face. The title is the first thing players see in the hub — make it a good one!

overviewDescription.title: Write a description
overviewDescription.body: The description shows on your card's detail page and supports Markdown. Explain the gameplay and highlights so players want to click in!

publish.title: Publish your world
publish.body: When you're ready, click here at the top right to submit for publishing. Once approved it appears in the hub for everyone to play!

save.title: Remember to save
save.body: Save any time here (Ctrl+S works too). A little dot on the button reminds you when there are unsaved changes.

studio.title: A different way to work
studio.body: The Canvas switch at the top left changes editors. Turn it on and the whole card is laid out on one board, every part a piece you can drag; on a desktop that is where a card opens by default, and this is the Full editor. Simple mode is in the ⋮ menu. Switch whenever you like.

menuAdvanced.title: More advanced sections
menuAdvanced.body: The menu also holds Custom UI, Audio and Assets — advanced tools for giving your card its own interface and soundtrack. Come back when you're comfortable; the Creator Guide has full tutorials!

saveM.title: Remember to save
saveM.body: Tap here at the top right to save any time. A little dot on the button reminds you when there are unsaved changes.

finish.title: Off you go!
finish.body: That's the whole lap! Hit PLAY any time to playtest your world. For a deeper dive, open the Creator Guide at the top right — and find me in the three-dot menu at the top to replay this tour. Have fun building!

kbBooksM.title: Scenarios
kbBooksM.body: This row holds the card's scenarios. The card itself is the first: everything you write goes in there, and it is shared into every scenario you add later. Add one when your story needs a second place. For now, write something into the card.

publishM.title: Publish your world
publishM.body: When you are ready, tap here to submit for publishing. Once approved it appears in the hub for everyone to play!

menuOpen.title: The section menu
menuOpen.body: Every area of the editor — First Message, Lorebook, Variables, Behaviors and more — lives in this menu. Tap it open!

menuPick.title: Enter First Message
menuPick.body: See? These are all the areas. Let us start with First Message — tap it to enter!

greetingWrite.title: Write the first line
greetingWrite.body: Type the opening your players will read — even one sentence is enough for now. The grey text is a writing guide; it disappears as soon as you start.

sWelcome.title: Welcome to the Simple Editor!
sWelcome.body:
I'm Mushie! This page is a short form: numbered cards from top to bottom.
Fill in the ones marked REQUIRED and you already have a playable card. Let's walk it together!

sCards.title: Cards, top to bottom
sCards.body: Each numbered card is one part of your world. REQUIRED ones must be filled; OPTIONAL ones can wait. The list on the right jumps straight to any card.

sCharName.title: Name your character
sCharName.body: First, the star of the show. Replace the placeholder name with a real one — type it here!

sPersona.title: Who are they?
sPersona.body: Appearance, background, personality — the grey text is a template you can follow. Concrete details beat vague adjectives: one memorable trait beats three generic ones.

sWorldview.title: The world around them
sWorldview.body: Where and when does this happen, and what are the rules? Optional, but a few lines here keep the AI consistent.

sStyle.title: How they talk
sStyle.body: Tell the AI how this character speaks and how you want the prose written. Sample sentences work better than descriptions.

sSettings.title: Extra settings
sSettings.body: Key items, past events, house rules — anything else the AI should always know. Most cards can skip this at first.

sGreeting.title: Write the opening
sGreeting.body: The first message is what players see when they arrive — it sets the tone and length of everything after. Type your opening here, even a sentence is fine!

sAbout.title: Describe your card
sAbout.body: One or two sentences shown on Discover. This is the pitch that makes people click in.

sSave.title: Save your work
sSave.body: Save any time here (Ctrl+S works too). A little dot on the button reminds you when there are unsaved changes.

sPlay.title: Try it yourself
sPlay.body: Hit Play to test your card as a player — the fastest way to see whether the character feels right.

sPublish.title: Publish
sPublish.body: When you're happy, submit for publishing here. Once approved it appears on Discover for everyone to play.

sAdvanced.title: Need more power?
sAdvanced.body: Variables, behaviors, lorebooks, custom UI — switch Canvas on to unlock the full engine. Switch any time; I'll be waiting there with another tour.

sAdvancedM.title: Need more power?
sAdvancedM.body: Scroll down: the Canvas unlocks variables, behaviors, lorebooks and custom UI. Switch any time; I'll be waiting there with another tour.

sFinish.title: You're all set!
sFinish.body:
That's the simple editor! Fill in the cards, hit Play to test, publish when ready.
Find me again in the three-dot menu at the top whenever you want a refresher.

backgrounds.blurb: A picture behind the chat. Text gets a dark layer over it so it stays readable.
backgrounds.emptyHint: Start with the cover you already have — no upload, no generation.

backgrounds.previewSentence: The rain pressed the whole city low. She did not look back — she only tilted the umbrella your way.

packs.title: Mechanic packs
packs.blurb: A working set of variables, behaviors and lore, added in one click. Everything it adds is ordinary card content — open it, read it, change it.
packs.deterministic: Real variables — the engine applies them, so switching model changes nothing.
packs.promptOnly: Prompt only — the model decides whether to comply. Use variables when it has to be exact.
packs.footnote: Packs stack — affection and survival can live on the same card. Remove one from the Bundles page and everything it brought goes with it.

variantTranslate.banner: This is the {{language}} version, but its content is still the original text. Translate it item by item, or let the assistant do it.
variantTranslate.ask: Ask the assistant to translate into {{language}}
variantTranslate.prompt: Translate this whole card into {{language}}: the title and description, every opening message, all entries (characters, world, settings), variable names and descriptions, what behaviors tell the AI, and the text on the interface. Keep the meaning, tone and personalities; adapt names the way {{language}} readers expect. Leave macros in curly braces and variable ids exactly as they are.

appPacks.title: In-story apps
appPacks.blurb: Apps the player opens from a dock beside the chat: messages, relationships, a feed, the clock… Each one keeps its data in one variable and the AI fills it in as the story goes — the preview above each card is the real app. You don't build anything.
appPacks.footnote: The app's words follow the card's language (Chinese, English or Spanish). Remove it from the Bundles page and its button, data and rules go with it.
